title: Nvidia’s Scarcity Runs Out in Five Years: ‘A Chip Designed by OpenAI, by AI’

questions.question: Will OpenAI move its Jalapeno chip from testing into deployment for inference workloads by December 31, 2027?
questions.why_it_matters: A real deployment would be evidence that a major AI customer can substitute its own silicon for NVIDIA GPUs in at least some workloads, potentially weakening NVIDIA’s competitive position and future demand. The article says Jalapeno is not expected to disrupt NVIDIA’s results this year or next, so the near-term question is whether it advances to deployment within the next calendar year—not whether it changes NVIDIA’s FY2027 revenue.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing question about Google TPU’s share of incremental chip units in calendar 2027 tracks Google’s unit share, not whether OpenAI’s distinct Jalapeno chip advances from tests to deployment. NVIDIA’s 2026 highest-end AI-chip market-share question also measures a different market outcome and period. Neither answer would determine whether Jalapeno is deployed.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check by December 31, 2027, an analyst check date; the article gives no Jalapeno deployment deadline. Review OpenAI announcements and credible reporting for confirmation that Jalapeno has moved beyond tests into use for inference workloads. Distinguish an announced plan or test result from actual deployment.

evidence.quote: OpenAI's new Jalapeno silicon "a chip designed by OpenAI, by AI" and "is not going to disrupt their numbers this year, it's not going to disrupt them next year."
evidence.what_it_shows: The article presents Jalapeno as a potential competitor but attributes the view that it will not affect NVIDIA’s results this year or next. This supports focusing on the milestone of deployment rather than treating near-term revenue disruption as established.
evidence.original_speaker: Jordi Visser, as quoted by the article.

evidence.quote: Chip analyst and 247 Wall Street contributor Eric Bleeker cited a SemiAnalysis headline reading "OpenAI Jalapeno better than Nvidia Blackwell," noting initial tests point to superior total cost of ownership compared to Blackwell.
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported initial tests and claimed total-cost-of-ownership advantage provide a possible economic rationale for OpenAI to deploy the chip. The article describes initial tests, not commercial deployment.

evidence.quote: Jim Cramer on CNBC added: "Nvidia invested 30 billion in OpenAI" and OpenAI is "downright gleeful about inventing this new chip, Jalapeno, that can compete with Nvidia's."
evidence.what_it_shows: The passage underscores the competitive significance of OpenAI developing a chip that can compete with NVIDIA’s, while also noting NVIDIA’s reported investment in OpenAI. It does not establish deployment.

evidence.quote: Chamath Palihapitiya made the structural case on All-In: "You're going to look at these big companies in five years, they're all going to have their own cloud, they're all going to have their own models, they're all going to have their own silicon, they're all going to have their own data centers."
evidence.what_it_shows: This is a broader view that large technology companies may build their own silicon, providing context for the potential competitive threat. It is a five-year prediction, not evidence that Jalapeno will be deployed by the proposed check date.

evidence.quote: Huang counters that OpenAI's existing and planned commitments represent approximately 12 gigawatts of NVIDIA compute through 2030, and AI-lab demand should contribute roughly a quarter of NVIDIA's business next year.
evidence.what_it_shows: This counterpoint indicates substantial stated OpenAI demand for NVIDIA compute through 2030 and the importance of AI-lab demand to NVIDIA next year. It weighs against assuming Jalapeno deployment would eliminate those commitments or demand; it does not resolve whether Jalapeno itself will be deployed.
evidence.original_speaker: Jensen Huang, as reported by the article.

evidence.quote: The terminal value debate is where the fight lives. If custom silicon peels off even a quarter of hyperscaler workloads by 2031, the DCF supporting today's price gets rewritten downward. If Vera Rubin's economics of $40 billion per gigawatt keep expanding, the moat holds.
evidence.what_it_shows: The journalist frames custom-silicon substitution as a possible threat to NVIDIA’s valuation and Vera Rubin’s economics as a possible defense. The 2031 workload scenario is beyond this question’s check period and is conditional, not a reported outcome.

evidence.quote: For NVIDIA investors, the forward question is direct. If Jalapeno and successors take even a slice of inference workloads by 2030, does the current multiple compress before fiscal 2028 growth arrives? Watch memory pricing, hyperscaler capex mix, and how quickly OpenAI's chips move from tests to deployment.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article explicitly identifies movement from testing to deployment as a relevant signal for investors. The 2030 inference-workload scenario is a conditional longer-term view; the proposed question focuses on whether deployment begins within the allowed next-calendar-year tracking horizon.

article:
NVDA posted $96 billion in Q2 revenue, up 106% year over year, but Visser warns its scarcity advantage disappears within five to six years.
OpenAI's Jalapeno already beats Blackwell on total cost of ownership, with Chamath predicting every major tech firm owns its own silicon in five years.
Eli Lilly shares surged 61% over one year partnering with NVDA on AI drug discovery, while COIN fell 21% year to date despite crossing $100 million in annualized prediction-markets revenue.
Two days after the biggest quarter in semiconductor history, macro investor Jordi Visser told listeners on The Pomp Podcast that the scarcity holding up NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) has an expiration date. His argument separates near-term results from terminal value, laid out in a single line: OpenAI's new Jalapeno silicon "a chip designed by OpenAI, by AI" and "is not going to disrupt their numbers this year, it's not going to disrupt them next year." Then the pivot: "Nvidia right now has scarcity, but at some point, five years from now, six years from now, it won't have scarcity." NVIDIA's market cap of $5.31 trillion reflects future discounted cash flows. If the market decides GPUs are optional in a decade, that value contracts.
NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 report delivered. Revenue landed at $96.22 billion, up 105.8% year over year, with Data Center revenue of $89.02 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $2.22. Supply commitments jumped to $279 billion, largely memory tied to Vera Rubin. See the Q2 FY2027 8-K exhibit for the full breakout.
Jensen Huang told analysts fiscal 2028 revenue should grow approximately 70% year over year, and that "at this moment, we have supply for 70%. We have more supply than 70%, but about 70%. Our demand is much higher than that." The stock dropped 4.57% on Aug 28, 2026, from $227.98 to $217.55, though shares are up 16.79% year to date and trade at a forward P/E of 26.
Chip analyst and 247 Wall Street contributor Eric Bleeker cited a SemiAnalysis headline reading "OpenAI Jalapeno better than Nvidia Blackwell," noting initial tests point to superior total cost of ownership compared to Blackwell. Jim Cramer on CNBC added: "Nvidia invested 30 billion in OpenAI" and OpenAI is "downright gleeful about inventing this new chip, Jalapeno, that can compete with Nvidia's."
Chamath Palihapitiya made the structural case on All-In: "You're going to look at these big companies in five years, they're all going to have their own cloud, they're all going to have their own models, they're all going to have their own silicon, they're all going to have their own data centers."
Huang counters that OpenAI's existing and planned commitments represent approximately 12 gigawatts of NVIDIA compute through 2030, and AI-lab demand should contribute roughly a quarter of NVIDIA's business next year. Visser agrees on the near term, calling the current setup "the sweet spot of the infrastructure build out" with "another three to five years of needing a lot."
The terminal value debate is where the fight lives. If custom silicon peels off even a quarter of hyperscaler workloads by 2031, the DCF supporting today's price gets rewritten downward. If Vera Rubin's economics of $40 billion per gigawatt keep expanding, the moat holds.
Eli Lilly ( NYSE:LLY ) cited a co-innovation AI lab with NVIDIA for drug discovery and posted $22.97 billion in Q2 revenue with EPS of $8.38, raising FY26 revenue guidance to $85.0 billion to $87.0 billion. LLY shares are up 61.49% over one year.
Coinbase ( NASDAQ:COIN ) shows the flip side: Q2 revenue fell 18.51% to $1.22 billion, and the stock is down 21% year to date even with prediction-markets revenue past $100 million annualized.
For NVIDIA investors, the forward question is direct. If Jalapeno and successors take even a slice of inference workloads by 2030, does the current multiple compress before fiscal 2028 growth arrives? Watch memory pricing, hyperscaler capex mix, and how quickly OpenAI's chips move from tests to deployment.
